$doc: The AgentOS design tokens: the single source of every colour, size, font and timing in docs/DESIGN.md. Edit this file, then run `pnpm --filter @agentos/design build`: it writes tokens.css (web), generated/Tokens.swift (iPhone, watch) and src/tokens.data.ts (TypeScript). Keys starting with $ are notes. Lengths are CSS pixels (points on Apple platforms), durations milliseconds, tracking em, springs { duration in seconds, bounce 0-1 }.

color.$doc: Every colour by its role, with its value on dark and on light surfaces. Everything follows the appearance except OS mode and the watch, which are always dark.

black.$doc: The watch and the screens OS mode covers: true black for OLED and Always On.

surface-stage.$doc: Where the presence lives: the home stage, the panel's header, phone home. A warm night in dark, warm daylight in light. OS mode stays dark.

surface.$doc: The page of a utility surface: panel, settings, onboarding, the conversation column.

surface-raised.$doc: Cards, groups of rows, bubbles, fields. Always with shadow-raised.

surface-overlay.$doc: Things that float: sheets, menus, toasts, the OS-mode request. Always with shadow-overlay.

line-strong.$doc: The edge of what is selected.

ring.$doc: The 1 px edge of a control: secondary buttons, fields, chips.

outline.$doc: Around pictures: pure white or black, never a tinted grey.

text-dim.$doc: Secondary text. Readable (4.5:1) on every surface.

text-faint.$doc: Placeholders and disabled labels: never something that must be read.

fill.$doc: A neutral control: secondary buttons, chips, fields, icon tiles.

fill-strong.$doc: The same under the pointer, or pressed.

primary.$doc: The primary button: pearl on dark, ink on light. Made of the presence's own idle colour.

primary-top.$doc: Top of the primary button's gradient (light from above).

primary-bottom.$doc: Bottom of the primary button's gradient.

primary-highlight.$doc: The 1 px inner light along the primary button's top edge.

on-primary.$doc: The label on a primary button.

primary-check.$doc: The check on Go ahead: the only colour on the primary button.

working.$doc: The agent is working: activity dots, progress, selection. Also the keyboard focus ring, as on every Mac.

waiting.$doc: The agent is asking. Nothing else is amber.

asking-light.$doc: The presence's light falling on a request: the card's top edge and corner wash. Decoration only, never text.

go.$doc: Done, approved: the check of Go ahead and of receipts. Icons only (3:1), never a button fill.

go-fill.$doc: Behind a check in a receipt.

careful.$doc: Be careful: high risk, errors, options marked danger. Red never means Stop.

careful-fill.$doc: Behind the high-risk banner and a careful button.

focus.$doc: The 2 px keyboard focus ring, 2 px away from the edge.

glass.$doc: The one material: controls that float over content (the phone composer, OS-mode controls). Never glass on glass.

alias.$doc: Old names kept working until every surface has moved to the new ones (see the handoff). Do not use them in new code.

presence.$doc: The presence's colours per state: the body's gradient (from top left to bottom right), its inner core (the brightest light inside the body), its glow (halo colour and strength). The renderer in packages/presence draws them; on light surfaces it turns to ink with a soft coloured glow for the coloured states.

idle.$doc: Pearl: resting, content. A warm white, not a cold one.

working.$doc: Lagoon: busy. Azure into aqua, like water, not the blue-violet every AI product uses.

waiting.$doc: Amber: the agent needs its owner.

listening.$doc: White with a cool edge: taking your words in.

speaking.$doc: White with a warm edge: giving words out.

offline.$doc: Warm grey, no glow: asleep, not broken.

via.$doc: A change between two coloured states travels through this light, never through the muddy mix of the two.

stage-light.$doc: The presence's light on the stage beneath it: its state colour at this opacity, in a radial gradient this many times the stage size. Off on the watch.

font.$doc: One family on the web, apps and website alike: Figtree (SIL Open Font License), self-hosted in fonts/, weights 300-600. Apple apps use the system font so that Dynamic Type, Bold Text and the watch work as people expect; the agent's voice there is SF Pro Rounded, the system face closest to Figtree's round forms.

web.brand: Figtree, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, system-ui, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
web.text: Figtree, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, system-ui, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
web.display: Figtree, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, system-ui, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
web.mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

apple.$doc: Font.Design of the system font for each voice.

type.$doc: Two voices. Display is the agent talking: Figtree 400 (360 when very large), tight, centred, one sentence. Text is the interface: 400 for reading, 600 for titles and buttons. Nothing a person must read is under 15 px; label and caption are for short tags only. `apple` is the Dynamic Type style each size follows.

display-xl.$doc: The agent's line in OS mode; the website's hero.

display-l.$doc: The line on the desktop home; the question in OS mode.

display-s.$doc: The line on a phone and in the panel; the question of a request on a phone.

title-l.$doc: Screen titles (Settings); the question of a request card on the desktop.

title.$doc: Section titles, sheet titles, the question of a request in the side panel and on the watch.

body-l.$doc: The agent's words in the conversation; leads on the website.

body-strong.$doc: Row titles, the owner's name for things.

small.$doc: Secondary text: row subtitles, details, helper lines.

label.$doc: Short labels: "Nova is asking", chips, section headers.

caption.$doc: Times and counts beside something larger. Never a sentence.

button.$doc: The label of a button up to 44 px high.

button-big.$doc: The label of a 52 px button and taller.

name-large.$doc: The agent's name above a large stage.

code.$doc: Commands, paths and addresses, inside Details and Advanced only.

space.$doc: The spacing scale, each step named after its length. Nothing in between: if 12 is too tight, use 16.

radius.$doc: Corner radii. Single-line controls are capsules (full). Nested corners are concentric: outer = inner + inset (xl 28 = m 16 + 12; xxl 36 = m 16 + 20; l 22 = s 10 + 12).

size.$doc: Fixed sizes. Anything a finger or a pointer can hit is at least `control` in both directions.

control.$doc: How a control answers a finger or a pointer.

elevation.$doc: Depth comes from light above: a higher surface is lighter, carries a 1 px top highlight and a soft shadow. Two levels at most on a screen.

material.$doc: The glass material's blur, and the presence's light on a request card (in asking-light).

stage.$doc: The side of the presence's stage on each surface: a fixed length, or a rule (a share of the height and of the width of the box it may use, kept between min and max). stageSize() applies it; the box is the window, or on home-beside the presence's own column.

os-asking.$doc: OS mode while asking: the presence rises above the request.

home.$doc: Home with the conversation below: a phone.

home-beside.$doc: Home with the conversation beside: a window.

motion.$doc: Durations for things that do not move (fades, colours), and springs for things that do. A spring is { duration, bounce }: the same numbers as SwiftUI's .spring(duration:bounce:) and motion's { type: "spring", visualDuration, bounce }. Position may bounce; colour and opacity never do. Everything is interruptible.

snappy.$doc: Icons swapping, chips, small state changes.

press.$doc: A control coming back after a press.

layout.$doc: Things changing size or place: a card folding into a receipt, a sheet, a row unfolding.

gesture.$doc: Things arriving with intent: a request card, a toast, a step of onboarding.

arrive.$doc: Content arriving: each chunk (title, text, actions) rises 12 px from 4 px blur and 0 opacity, 60 ms after the previous one.

leave.$doc: Content leaving: shorter and quieter than arriving.

icon-swap.$doc: One icon turning into another: both stay, cross-fading in scale, blur and opacity.

resolve.$doc: Answering a request: the chosen button's icon becomes a check at 0 ms; the other button fades at 120 ms; the card folds into its receipt at 600 ms (layout spring), once the answer has been seen.

line.$doc: The agent's line changing: the old one fades out (ease in), then the new one fades in (ease out). Never two at once.

haptic.$doc: One meaning per haptic, on the iPhone and the watch. Haptics mark confirmed outcomes, not taps.
